environmental_laws.name: CERCLA / Superfund (42 U.S.C. ? 9601 et seq.)
environmental_laws.legal_power: Joint, Several, and Strict Liability for Potentially Responsible Parties (PRPs), mandatory National Priorities List (NPL) site cleanup, and public health risk assessments.

environmental_laws.name: RCRA (Resource Conservation and Recovery Act, 42 U.S.C. ? 6901)
environmental_laws.legal_power: Cradle-to-Grave tracking of hazardous waste generation, transport manifests, treatment, storage, and disposal (TSDF).

environmental_laws.name: California Carpenter-Presley-Tanner Hazardous Substance Account Act (HSAA, Cal. Health & Safety Code ? 25300 et seq.)
environmental_laws.legal_power: State-level Superfund enforcement, mandatory remedial action plans (RAPs), cost recovery, and land deed environmental restrictions (institutional controls).

environmental_laws.name: Porter-Cologne Water Quality Control Act (Cal. Water Code ? 13000 et seq.)
environmental_laws.authority: California Regional Water Quality Control Boards (RWQCB)
environmental_laws.legal_power: Cleanup and Abatement Orders (CAOs), Waste Discharge Requirements (WDRs), and regulation of produced water, sumps, and aquifer recharge protection.

environmental_laws.name: CEQA Mandatory Environmental Impact Reports (EIRs, Cal. Pub. Res. Code ? 21000 et seq.)
environmental_laws.legal_power: Requires disclosure of known hazardous materials sites under Government Code ? 65962.5 (Cortese List) prior to development or rezoning approval.

corporate_actors.role: Hazardous Waste Hauling, Incineration, Chemical Treatment & TSDF Operation
corporate_actors.key_operations: Operates major hazardous waste Class I landfills (e.g., Buttonwillow, Westmorland) receiving toxic excavation soils from coastal redevelopment sites.

corporate_actors.role: Industrial Landfill Operation & Remediation Soil Disposal
corporate_actors.key_operations: Historical operators of municipal and industrial waste disposal sites in Southern California (including former Republic disposal pits).

corporate_actors.company_name: AECOM / Jacobs Engineering / Tetra Tech / Geosyntec Consultants
corporate_actors.role: Environmental Engineering, Remedial Investigation/Feasibility Study (RI/FS), Soil Vapor Mitigation
corporate_actors.key_operations: Contracted by municipal agencies, oil companies, and developers to perform Phase I/II Environmental Site Assessments, pump-and-treat systems, slurry walls, and remediation certification.

corporate_actors.company_name: Cannery Oceanic & Oilfield PRP Groups (Shell, Chevron, ExxonMobil, ConocoPhillips)
corporate_actors.role: Historical Polluters & Superfund Responsible Party Consortia
corporate_actors.key_operations: Legacy petroleum extraction, produced water discharge sumps, styrene and drilling mud pit operations subject to DTSC consent decrees.

gis_data_footprint.what_it_maps: Exact polygon boundaries of Superfund sites (Ascon Landfill), voluntary cleanups, corrective actions, contaminants of concern (VOCs, Lead, Benzene, PCBs), cleanup progress, and deed restriction covenants.
Leaking Underground Storage Tanks (LUST), Landfills, Land Disposal Sites, Oilfield Produced Water Sumps, and monitoring well contamination test points.
Consolidated mandatory disclosure list for local governments prior to issuing development permits. Properties on this list cannot use CEQA categorical exemptions.

gis_data_footprint.dataset_name: City of Huntington Beach Municipal GIS (Parcels, Stormwater BMPs, Utilities)
gis_data_footprint.what_it_maps: Stormwater BMP treatment locations (StormwaterBMPs), city sewer/storm lines (SewerLayers, StormLayers), and parcel zoning (Planning). However, explicit toxic plume outlines and private remediation manifests are typically omitted from public-facing city maps to prevent real estate devaluation.

fca_arbitrage_nexus.mechanism: The Toxic Remediation & Property Flipping Arbitrage Loop
steps: 1. Concealment: City & private developers obtain Phase II ESA reports showing severe VOC/heavy metal plumes but do not record deed restrictions immediately.
2. Acquisition at Depressed Cost: Connected entities buy distressed/blighted property at 70-80% discount citing "environmental uncertainty".
3. Public Subsidy Cleanup: Entities obtain state/federal Brownfields grants or municipal infrastructure funds to pay remediation contractors (Clean Harbors/Tetra Tech).
4. Reclassification & Rezoning: Once public funds clean the upper soil layer, the city re-zones the tract to high-density luxury residential/commercial, creating massive unearned equity.
